text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Thursday:
- Swiss World Airways, a new Swiss airline, has plans to offer long distance flights overseas departing from Geneva as of October. It will begin flying with two Boeing 767s.
- "Basel 97", the annual watch and jewelry trade show, begins today and features 2,300 exhibitors from 35 countries.
- Winterthur Insurance Group named Thomas Wellauer, currently a director at McKinsey & Company in Zurich, its new CEO.
- The largest Jewish community in Switzerland is demanding that the Swiss government appoint Rolf Bloch, currently its president, as the head of the newly created funds for Holocaust victims.
- Switzerland exported 1.6 percent fewer watches- a total of 7.551 billion Swiss francs - in 1996 compared to the previous year.
- Sarna Group's 1996 sales rose by 20 percent to 572.1 million Swiss francs.
- Shares in Selecta, a vending machine company and subsidiary of the Valora Group, will be traded at the stock exchange starting May 12.
- Retail sales firm Denner's net profit rose from 2.8 million Swiss francs for 1994 to 5.2 million in 1996.

- The Federal Department for Civilian Air Transportation said Swissair has too many foreigners on its board, which is against the Swiss aviation law. It has four Swiss and three non-Swiss board members. Swissair said it would solve the problem.
- United Nations Secretary General Kofi Annan said he is in favor of setting up a main office for human rights in the Wilson Palace in Geneva.
